text.p: LME copper was locked in a narrow range on Monday afternoon, taking a rest after attacking the $2,600 per tonne mark last week.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 0.92 points to 243.53.
On the LME, yhird Wednesday pricing during the morning rings failed to spark much excitement and three month copper finished the afternoon kerb little changed at $2,588, down $2 from Friday.
The other metals followed copper's lead, lazily testing the downside.
Nickel chalked up a loss of $90, ending at $7,250, failing to respond to problems at Inco and Norilsk.
Aluminium was trapped in a tight $8 range between $1,577 and $1,585, ending right in the middle at $1,582, a loss of $4 from Friday's close.
Lead declined by $8 to $621 and may be heading towards its recent $615 lows, traders said.
Tin shed $20 to $5,560 and zinc ended $1 weaker at $1,373.
Alloy finished the kerb $5 easier indicated at $1,475/80.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on rains in the U.S. spring wheat growing region and new crop July hit a four-month low, traders said. Traders and analysts also cited the lack of large scale export business as bearish to the market. Wheat closed 2-1/2 to 10-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 9-3/4 at $3.42-3/4.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Monday, with gold and silver higher on light volume and platinum and palladium lower. COMEX August gold ended up $1.70 at $344.80 an ounce after trading from $342.90 to $345.00 on estimated total COMEX gold volume of only 9,000 lots. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $342.40/90 against the London afternoon fix of $341.50 and the New York finish Friday of $340.80/$341.30.

North Sea benchmark Brent crude gained ground in late U.S. paper trading on Monday in a string of partial transactions, traders said. Partial August cargoes changed hands seven times between $17.85 and $17.91, rounding out the aftermarket at $17.87-90 a barrel. London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) closed at $17.86 for August. September settled at $18.04.
